subject: Implementation plan: No-train opt-out, prompt/response ownership, and subprocessor routing
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@blueriverhealth.com>; Marco Alvarez <marco.alvarez@blueriverhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Nov 2024 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Implementation plan: No-train opt-out, prompt/response ownership, and subprocessor routing

Hi Elena / Marco —

Thanks for the productive call this morning. As discussed, BlueRiver is asking for a concrete operational plan to support your DPA amendment: (1) a binding no-training (no-model-improvement) commitment for tenant data, (2) clear prompt/response ownership and export options, and (3) routing rules for any subprocessors (onshore vs. offshore handling).

Action items I promised to deliver in this thread:
- A short operational playbook describing how Redwood will enforce a no-train opt-out at the request/tenant level (what toggles, audits, evidence we provide).
- A mapping of subprocessors and routing rules we will apply for BlueRiver traffic (S3/SFTP/KMS residency).
- A customer-facing checklist to attest to deletion/retention and a sample evidence pack.

Attached: a draft "no-train optout playbook" and a routing map (work-in-progress). Please review and flag anything missing.

Quick clarifications up-front:
- Opt-out scope: includes any model-improvement pipelines and offline training. It excludes aggregated anonymized telemetry used for product health metrics (we can enumerate these if you want).
- Prompt/response ownership: BlueRiver retains IP in prompts and the model outputs they generate; Redwood will not assert derivative rights. We will also provide an export of logs/on-demand transcripts for audit (sftp/secure api).
- Evidence: we can provide signed attestation, per-request headers showing opt-out tags, and an ops export with timestamps and KMS key ids. For EU residency we can route exclusively to eu-1 pools if needed.

Neha / David / Kimberly — can you confirm the operational steps below are accurate and note any gaps?

Planned operational steps (high level):
1) Tenant flag: add boolean tenant-level flag (no_model_learning) that is evaluated at the routing layer. Default: false. Timeline: 2 weeks for feature toggle + 1 week for QA.
2) Runtime enforcement: if flag=true, runtime sets a non-learning enforcement header and blocks any traffic to training pipelines. Timeline: immediate config change after flag is live.
3) Logging & evidence: capture per-request metadata (tenant id, request id, timestamp, KMS key id, routing node). Ops export weekly + ad-hoc on request.
4) Subprocessor routing: update routing policy to prefer onshore/subscribed pools for flagged tenants; fallback to dedicated onshore burst pools only after capacity checks.
5) Export package: SFTP package + signed attestation PDF delivered on request; DocuSign template to acknowledge no-train commitment.

Let me know if you'd like a short walkthrough call after you review the attachments.

Thanks,
Rishi
--
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Privacy & Compliance (Contracts)
Redwood Inference

---

From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@blueriverhealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Alvarez <marco.alvarez@blueriverhealth.com>; Tara Jenkins <tara.jenkins@legalwise.co>; Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>; Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Nov 2024 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Implementation plan: No-train opt-out, prompt/response ownership, and subprocessor routing

Thanks Rishi — this is very helpful. A couple of clarifying asks from legal and security before we sign off: 

1) Can you confirm the attestation will include the exact runtime timestamps and KMS key ids for the requests included in an export? Security wants cryptographic metadata where available.
2) For prompt/response ownership, we need a clause that explicitly prevents Redwood (and subprocessors) from using tenant outputs for model updates or derivative training even in aggregate. Is the runtime header enforcement sufficient for contract language, or do you recommend an additional contractual warranty?
3) Subprocessor routing: we need a clearer escalation path if onshore pools are at capacity and traffic temporarily routes to a cross-border pool — what notifications do we provide and what is the maximum allowed duration?

Once we have answers to the three bullets above, legal can review the amendment language.

Best,
Elena
Director, Data Governance
BlueRiver Health

---

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@blueriverhealth.com>, Marco Alvarez <marco.alvarez@blueriverhealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Nov 2024 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Implementation plan: No-train opt-out, prompt/response ownership, and subprocessor routing

Elena — quick answers from ops/security side below. Happy to jump on a call if helpful.

1) Evidence & KMS metadata: yes — exports will include request-level timestamps, request ids, and KMS key fingerprints (where applicable). We will also include a signed manifest (SHA256) of the export bundle and a statement of custody signed by our SOC team.

2) Contract + runtime enforcement: runtime header + tenant flag is our primary technical control. For legal comfort we recommend a contractual warranty that references the runtime enforcement plus an operational attestation clause (we will commit to provide evidence on request within the SLA window). We cannot guarantee 100% prevention against every novel training pipeline (there are always edge cases), but we will commit to remediate any deviation discovered and provide full forensic logs.

Suggested language (high level): 
- Redwood warrants that, for opt-out tenants, Redwood will not (and will cause its subprocessors not to) use customer content or outputs to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any models, and will enforce this via tenant-level runtime controls.
- Redwood will provide on-request export and signed attestation within 5 business days.

3) Onshore capacity fallback: Ops suggests the following escalation & visibility path: 
- Policy: route to onshore (us) pools only. If onshore capacity < 10% and queue time exceeds configured SLO, traffic may be routed to a pre-approved cross-border dedicated pool with explicit tags and a max duration of 6 hours per incident.
- Notifications: automated email + Slack to BlueRiver's security alias and a weekly incident summary if any cross-border routing occurred.
- Manual escalation: if routing is expected to exceed the 6-hour cap, Ops will pause cross-border routing and initiate manual approval within 1 hour.

David / Kimberly — can you confirm implementation timelines (feature flag, evidence export endpoint, signed manifest) and whether the 6-hour temporary fallback is operationally achievable?

Thanks,
Neha
Director, Operations
Redwood Inference

---

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Elena Soto <elena.soto@blueriverhealth.com>, Marco Alvarez <marco.alvarez@blueriverhealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Nov 2024 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Implementation plan: No-train opt-out, prompt/response ownership, and subprocessor routing

All — operational confirmation below and a small change request for legal.

- Feature flag (no_model_learning): we can deliver the tenant-level flag and the runtime enforcement header in 10 business days (feature dev + 3-day QA + infra rollout).
- Evidence export: SFTP package with signed manifest can be produced within 5 business days of a request; the export will include per-request metadata and KMS ids.
- Onshore capacity fallback: 6-hour cap is reasonable. Implementation detail: we will add automatic tagging so any routed request has a cross-border tag and an incident id. The automated notification (email + Slack) will fire on the first cross-border routing event per day; a daily digest will follow.

Change request for legal: Instead of an open-ended remediation warranty clause, ops asks that the legal language includes a discovery-and-remediation timeline (e.g., Redwood will investigate any suspected use within 3 business days and remediate/provide a full forensic report within 15 business days). This helps set clear SLAs for operational processes.

Next steps: I will update the playbook doc with dev timelines and handoff notes, push a new routing map with tagging details, and share a draft amendment clause for the warranty + discovery SLA. Rishi / Neha — I can have those updates by Monday.

-David

Attachments: no-train-optoout-playbook.pdf (draft); subprocessor-routing-map.xlsx (WIP)
